title: Now check your own accounts
drDigitalIntro:
You have judged phishing messages, built strong passwords and used two-factor codes in practice. Now check your real accounts.
• Pick your most important account — email or banking — and turn on two-factor authentication if it is not already on.
• Change any password you use in more than one place. Reused passwords are the single biggest risk most people carry.
• Look at the last suspicious message you received and find the real address behind the link, without clicking it.
• If you are ever unsure, close the message and go to the company's website yourself. That habit alone prevents most scams.
drDigitalSuccess: These four habits protect you more than any software you could install.
drDigitalHint: Read along, then check one of your own accounts.
